finding.summary: The SSM assertions expect Value to be `{ Ref: <resource logical id> }`, but the stack sets explicit physical names (tableName, bucketName), so CDK synthesizes the SSM parameter values as plain strings: the table param's Value is the literal `pmat_<env>_ALPHA_MESH_REVIEW_CHECKPOINTS` (the exact same string the first test asserts as the table's TableName), and the bucket param's Value is an Fn::Join of the name prefix and the AWS::AccountId pseudo-parameter (the test app passes no env, so this.account is a token). Neither can ever equal `{ Ref: tableId }` / `{ Ref: bucketId }`, so the 'publishes table, bucket and ttl-days to SSM' test fails for both dev and prod (same defect at line 68).
finding.fix: Assert the values CDK actually emits: for the table, `Value: `pmat_${deployEnv}_ALPHA_MESH_REVIEW_CHECKPOINTS``; for the bucket, pass an explicit env (e.g. env: { account: '123456789012', region: 'us-east-1' }) when constructing the stack in synth() so this.account is concrete, then assert the full literal bucket name `pmat-${deployEnv}-alpha-mesh-review-checkpoints-123456789012`. The logicalId() helper can then be dropped from this test (it is still used by the IAM test).
